articles.title: Sebi proposes new CAS framework, two options for expiry-day settlement
articles.content: The Securities and Exchange Board of India (SEBI) is set to implement crucial updates to the Closing Auction Session. A focus of these changes is on the process of derivatives settlement on expiry days. SEBI has laid out two alternatives for determining the derivatives settlement price: the first proposes a blended VWAP approach after one year, while the second keeps the current CTS VWAP process in place for the present.

articles.title: US consumer prices accelerate in August, push Fed closer to rate hike

Rising energy costs have affected multiple sectors, with consumers bracing for higher inflation expectations that may dampen economic sentiment. The Federal Reserve now faces increased pressure to manage rising costs and ensure price stability.

articles.title: Indian rupee weakens to 95.55 amid rising crude oil prices and Strait of Hormuz tensions
articles.content: The Indian rupee fell by eleven paise on Friday, closing at 95.55 against the dollar as benchmark crude oil prices rose to $105 per barrel, fueling global uncertainties. The rupee faced mounting pressure from external factors during the week, with a notable demand for dollars from oil companies and dollar sales from state-run banks. It appears that the Reserve Bank of India stepped in to mitigate further currency depreciation.

Factors such as high global risk-free rates and escalating crude oil prices are exerting pressure on Indian bonds.

articles.title: Bank deposits grow 17.8% in August, fastest in decade as FCNR-B inflows mask local mobilisation woes
articles.content: Bank deposits grew 17.8% year-on-year at the end of August, the fastest pace in a decade, driven largely by a surge in FCNR-B deposits after RBI opened a special window for dollar inflows. Credit growth eased slightly to 19.1%, while banks continued to face challenges in mobilising domestic savings.
